There may be less stupid jokes at the top, and opinions may be less idiotic, but at the end of the day, it results in circlejerking and censorship on the level of reddit. The first handful of comments posted will remain at the top for eternity, as long as they are liked by the majority of people, and everything else below will be unseen except by a few people who have the time and interest to scroll through everything.

I often read posts about how discussions on Voat are different than many you find elsewhere in that disagreeing parties tend to be more civil with one another (though this is certainly not universal). Either way, there seems to be far more people willing to engage in discussion, and encouraging that would be amazing for the sight.

The problem you so often find is that the those with unpopular opinions get downvoated (surprising, I know). But being able to engage with people who don't share your views is really important in getting people to think critically. Some incredible discussions can take place and have seen threads where where downvoated posts contained well thought out, civil debates that simply end up at the bottom of the list because a handful of people disagreed earlier.

We've also seen the flip of this situation where a wise-assed, funny comment dominates a discussion board just because it's amusing and short. The issue seems to be that there is no definitive use for the upvoat or downvoat buttons; they might mean you agree, might mean you think the comment is important, might mean you laughed, who knows.

Both of these things could be remedied with a separate, more specific voating system for determining the comments importance. In the first instance, people may see the original comment as something that they disagree with/whatever reason they downvoat for. But then they see a reply that they believe perfectly responds to the original comment in a way the user thinks would be valuable to see. The user could downvoat the opinion, but upvoat the comment so as to keep the whole conversation ready for others to see. In the second instance, people would be able to give the reputation points to the clever comment while leaving it low in the overall queue. CCP still changes in the same way but here a conversation has a chance to flourish even if not a popular opinion.
Idea: A way to give CCP for a comment without changing its rank when browsing top comments?
